title: node-heartbeat-fanout-lease-renewal-spiral-investigation
content:
Summary:

Short description: Brief notes from the on-call and follow-up investigation into a recurring cluster availability blip starting 2024-11-18 03:42 UTC. Symptoms were elevated api-server CPU, high etcd leader CPU on small write bursts, and a backlog of Pending pods in the default queue. Impact: several user-facing jobs experienced 10–30s pod start delays; one managed customer saw >1 minute cold-starts on bursty jobs.

High-level hypothesis (quick TL;DR):
- A change in kubelet node-status churn combined with a periodic lease renewal fanout created a control-plane request spike.
- The spike manifested as small, repeated write-heavy operations against etcd (status updates), amplified by a k8s controller loop and a noisy custom node-exporter health probe.
- api-server CPU throttled p95 admission latency; scheduler experienced queue starvation for ~60s windows.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2024-11-18 03:42: incoming alert: api-server horizontal pod autoscaler CPU up 2x (pager)
- 03:43: SRE oncall ack, added to incident channel, grabbed first logs
- 03:45: Observed spike in /api/v1/nodes/*/status write QPS to api-server (from ~120/s to ~840/s for 2 min)
- 03:47: etcd leader CPU jumped, compact loops deferred; etcd WAL fsync p99 increased
- 03:49: Scheduler p95 binding latency rose, backlog of unsched pods appeared
- 03:52: api-server pods auto-scaled up (HPA) but new pods still saturated during spike
- 04:10: Spike subsided, metrics returned to baseline; follow-up channel created

Observations / evidence:
- api-server logs: frequent 200 writes to nodes/status endpoints, each ~1.2 KB. Example path: POST /api/v1/nodes/<node>/status -> consistent pattern 12s burst repeating across node set.
- Etcd metrics: increased apply duration, leader CPU 85% -> 95% during peak; commit duration p95 jumped from 14ms -> 312ms.
- Kubelet metrics: heartbeats showed synchronized bump; many nodes reported status update jitter aligning to a ~12s periodicity.
- Recent config change: cluster autoscaling of node-exporter probes combined with Prometheus scrape_interval reduction (PR merged 2024-11-10) — changed default scrape interval from 30s to 10s for node-exporter.
- Custom health probe: a small node healthsidecar performing a PUT to /status every scrape (legacy behavior). This produced writes to node/status on every scrape.

Root cause (working hypothesis):
1) Prometheus scrape interval reduction caused node-exporter and custom healthsidecar to run at 10s instead of 30s.
2) The sidecar issues triggered a synchronous write path that invoked node status updates (kubelet -> api-server).
3) Because many nodes were roughly in-phase (small clock drift + restart wave after a separate maintenance window earlier that night), the writes lined up causing a fanout spike to the api-server.
4) The spike increased etcd leader pressure which increased apply latency and briefly saturated api-server worker threads, causing scheduler starvation.

Why scheduler starved: scheduler depends on timely watch/update propagation and CPU for predicate/evaluator loops. When api-server worker threads were busy serving status writes and etcd apply slowed, the scheduler loop observed delayed list/watch events and binding loops slowed down. This increased scheduling latency until the write fanout decayed.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Temporarily raised api-server request timeouts and rotated one api-server pod to drain local cache and rebalance worker threads (manual delete -> k8s recreated).
- Increased etcd leader's IO priority by moving leader to a node with spare disk IOPS (manual failover using etcdctl member remove/add was considered but not executed).
- Rolled back the Prometheus scrape_interval to 30s in the monitoring namespace for node-exporter only (quick emergency revert).
- Short-term rate-limited node-status updates via admission controller not feasible during incident window.

Permanent fix candidates and recommendations:
- Fix the root cause in the health sidecar: stop performing synchronous PUTs to node/status on each scrape. Convert to asynchronous telemetry export or reduce frequency to >30s. Owner: Diego Ramos, due 2024-11-25.
- Add server-side throttling for node.status writes in api-server via an admission webhook that coalesces frequent updates or returns 429 under high load. Longer term: upstream KEP on node-status coalescing. Owner: Priya Khatri, due 2025-01-10.
- Audit Prometheus scrape targets for any call paths that result in control-plane writes. Enforce a monitoring-policy doc with guidelines for scrape intervals that touch control-plane resources. Owner: Monitoring team (Markus Levine), due 2024-12-01.
- Add smoothing to kubelet heartbeat timings: randomize initial heartbeat jitter and add a small per-node jitter on status updates (config suggestion in kubelet flags). Owner: eng-cluster-ops, due 2024-12-07.
- Create an SLO-aligned api-server autoscaling test harness to replay synthetic node-status fanout at different frequencies and measure et cetera apply latency. Owner: SRE Tools, due 2025-02-01.

Runbook edits (proposed quick text to add):
- Detection: alert if node/status write QPS rises >3x baseline for >60s AND etcd leader apply latency p95 >100ms.
- Immediate actions: temporarily raise scrape_interval for monitoring namespace; cordon one or two nodes producing the highest write rate to reduce immediate fanout; rotate api-server pods.
- Short-circuit: scale etcd cluster (add a follower with larger disk IOPS) only if apply latency p95 >250ms and sustained >5 minutes. Use runbook step with exact etcdctl commands.
- Post-incident: gather list of any services that perform writes during scrapes and require code changes.

Quick runbook checklist snippet (commands and hints):
- Check write QPS: kubectl -n kube-system exec -it $(kubectl get po -n kube-system -l component=kube-apiserver -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep apiserver_request_total | grep "/api/v1/nodes"
- Etcd leader metrics: curl -s http://etcd-metrics:2379/metrics | grep etcd_server_apply_duration_seconds
- Identify noisy nodes: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, lastStatus:.status.conditions[]? | select(.type=="Ready") | .lastTransitionTime}' (follow with kubelet logs grep for status PUTs)
- Rotate api-server: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/kube-apiserver (or drain one API pod if static).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why were nodes sufficiently in-phase? We expect jitter to desynchronize; hypothesis: many nodes restarted within a tight window due to a separate maintenance job earlier that night. Need to correlate restart events.
- Could a control-plane admission/webhook misconfiguration be amplifying writes? We saw no evidence yet, but audit logs need deeper inspection.
- Should we change default Prometheus scrape policy globally? Need cross-team governance.

Follow-ups and owners (action items):
- Diego Ramos: patch sidecar to stop PUT on scrape, create PR; due 2024-11-25.
- Markus Levine: audit monitoring jobs and add a monitoring policy doc; due 2024-12-01.
- Priya Khatri: prototype admission webhook for write coalescing; present KEP to eng-sre; due 2025-01-10.
- SRE Tools: build synthetic fanout test harness and run on staging; due 2025-02-01.
- Eng-cluster-ops: add kubelet heartbeat jitter to default node bootstrap config and ship across clusters; due 2024-12-07.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a working investigation draft. Evidence links are in the linked_artifacts field. We deliberately reverted monitoring config as the fast mitigation; full revert PR will include a description and a test plan to avoid future manual reverts. Please add any missing commands you used during oncall in the runbook snippet above so the later automation team can codify kill-switch actions.

Appendix: shortifer diagnostics paste (redacted):
- sample api-server metrics around spike: apiserver_request_total{resource="nodes",verb="update",client="kubelet"} increased from 112/s to 854/s at 03:45
- etcd apply duration p95: 312ms at 03:47
- kube-scheduler scheduling_latencies_seconds_bucket p95 moved from 48ms -> 1.2s during spike
- grep from kubelet logs on noisy-node-42: "PUT /api/v1/nodes/noisy-node-42/status 200 12.3ms" repeating every 10s

End of notes.
